summary: SSO approval redirect mismatch prevents ephemeral-service elevation for automation-runner
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Developer requests ephemeral 'automation-runner' elevation via /console/elevate endpoint
2) Console redirects user to Okta for device approval as usual
3) After approving the request in Okta, user is returned to /auth/callback with state and code
4) Instead of completing token exchange, user sees 403 'elevation denied' and is left on a blank intermediate redirect page
5) Retry attempts show same behavior across multiple accounts and browsers; CLI token exchange also fails with 'invalid_redirect_uri'.
logs: console-auth: 2026-03-12T17:04:12Z WARN callback-handler unexpected state mismatch for requestId=run-9b3f
token-service: 2026-03-12T17:04:12Z ERROR token-exchange failed invalid_redirect_uri client_id=svc-automation-runner
nginx-ingress: 2026-03-12T17:04:12Z INFO upstream returned 403 for /auth/callback from 10.12.3.44
investigation_notes: Initial triage by L2 support: replicated with multiple staff accounts; not limited to a single user or browser session.
Observed token-service rejecting exchange with 'invalid_redirect_uri' while Okta shows success on approval side.
Correlation found: a recent deployment (2026-03-11) modified redirect URI normalization in the auth gateway; change included trimming trailing slashes for legacy clients.

automation-runner uses a non-standard callback path '/auth/callback?client=automation-runner' and Okta is sending the full param-augmented URI back; normalization removed query string leading to mismatch against registered redirect for svc-automation-runner.

Config cross-check: Okta app for svc-automation-runner lists redirect URI as 'https://console.redwood.ai/auth/callback?client=automation-runner' (with query). Auth gateway now compares only path without query, resulting in token-service seeing a mismatched URI and returning invalid_redirect_uri.
Temporary reproduction: toggling gateway normalization off restores expected behavior for replicated flows.
Potential risk: all ephemeral elevation flows for automation-runner and any client that uses query-based redirect binding are impacted in us-west prod.
SRE note: routing and TLS unaffected; this is an auth-matching logic regression, not network failure.
comments: Support (Alicia Moreno) 2026-03-12: Customer-impacting: multiple engineers cannot get ephemeral tokens for CI/CD jobs. Escalating to Identity team.
Identity (Devon Park) 2026-03-12: Repro steps confirmed. Rolling back auth-gateway normalization in staging to verify. Assigning to me for hotfix path.
SRE (Priya Shah) 2026-03-13: Observability: no increase in 5xx for other endpoints. We can do a targeted rollback of the gateway change on the auth cluster in us-west.
Engineering (Marco Li) 2026-03-13: Quick fix prepared in PR #fix/normalize-redirect-query-preserve. Will liaise with Identity for safe rollout.
Support (Alicia Moreno) 2026-03-14: Confirmed workaround documented and communicated to oncall and impacted teams. Customer-facing impact mitigated via short-lived rollback.
resolution: Hotfix: Reverted redirect normalization change in auth-gateway on us-west auth cluster (rollback 2026-03-13 22:10 UTC). Identity adjusted token-service validation to accept query-preserved redirects for registered clients with explicit query parameters. Deployed patch and ran smoke tests for elevation flows. Full verification completed 2026-03-14. No further 403s reported for affected flows.
follow_up: 1) Create unit tests covering redirect URIs with query parameters (assigned Marco Li). 2) Audit Okta app registrations for other clients that rely on query-anchored redirects (assigned Identity team). 3) Add a Canary check in CI to validate ephemeral elevation flows after auth gateway deploys. Target completion: 2026-03-21.
